title: Residents skate the streets as freezing rain blankets Fort St. John, B.C.
summary: Warned to stay home due to hazardous roads, some northern British Columbians strapped on their skates instead Thursday morning, as freezing rain blanketed Fort St. John.

image.caption: Some Fort St. John residents took to the streets on skates and sleds after freezing rain blanketed roads the morning of Nov. 26, 2026. (Chris Boehm/Leann Muggeridge/Nicole Marshall)

blocks.text: Warned to stay home due to hazardous roads, some northern British Columbians strapped on their skates instead Thursday morning, as freezing rain blanketed Fort St. John.
Warned to stay home due to hazardous roads, some northern British Columbians strapped on their skates instead
Chris Boehm didn't let hazardous weather keep him indoors Thursday morning.
After freezing rain coated the streets of Fort St. John in northeast B.C., he decided to strap on his skates and take a spin around his neighbourhood.
"I saw a couple people skate by our house, I'm like, what the heck, I've never done this in my lifetime. I'm 50 years old, now I've done it," he said.
He wasn't alone. Around the city people took out their sleds, skates and hockey sticks to take advantage of the unusual conditions.
Residents skate and sled the icy roads of Fort St. John
"It was super fun, I felt like a kid again," said Leann Muggeridge, whose kids stayed home from school after bus runs were cancelled due to the slippery streets.
She said the roads were surprisingly smooth, likely due to a lack of snow, while Boehm said it was as if they had been flooded specifically for skating.

Throughout the morning, highway warnings were posted encouraging people not to drive unless absolutely necessary. The City of Fort St. John also urged people to avoid unnecessary travel as crews worked to clear and sand main routes.
"I know we have our ups and downs ... but I feel like when something like this happens you'll see even adults, their personalities come out," she said.
